name: qr-code
title: QR code
description: A QR code as crisp SVG from any string, drawn by a bundled encoder with four error correction levels, a quiet zone and SVG and PNG download.
docs: value is any string, sent as UTF-8. The encoder is bundled (pure TypeScript, versions 1 to 40, no package and no request): it picks the smallest version that holds the text in the densest mode the text allows, adds Reed-Solomon error correction and keeps the mask a scanner reads most easily. The code is one SVG path, so it is sharp at any size and prints well, and it is always dark modules on a white tile in both themes, because a scanner needs that contrast. size is the width of the tile in px (never wider than its container). level is L, M (default), Q or H: about 7, 15, 25 and 30 percent of the code may be lost, and a higher level is denser. margin is the quiet zone in modules (4, which scanners want). The figure is named after what it leads to, 'QR code for northwind.example/invite', from title or from value without its scheme. With actions a row offers Download SVG (a vector file at least 512px wide, on whole pixels per module, so Figma, Word or Keynote import it at a usable size) and Download PNG; the PNG is drawn from the SVG only when its button is pressed, on whole pixels per module and at least pngSize wide (1024), and onDownload(format, file) is called after either download starts (pass it from a client component). An empty value, or one too long for any code (7089 digits, 4296 capital letters or 2953 bytes at level L), shows a message in place of the tile. encodeQr(value, level) gives the modules for your own drawing and qrSvg(matrix, margin, pixels) a whole SVG document (with pixels it has a width and height). Only the download buttons need a script.
